    Docs/Connector.sln/Connector.Core/src-Connector.Core-DataSources
    Module

    src/Connector.Core/DataSources

    Layer domain · project Connector.Core

    Project navigation: Connector.Core

    Overview 🤖

    Manages data source configurations, capabilities, and operations for various ERP data sources.

    Responsibilities. Provides a unified interface for interacting with different ERP data sources, including validation, connection testing, and query execution.

    Usage. Used by various parts of the application to interact with different ERP data sources, ensuring consistent data access and management.

    AI draft from the facts on this page; review it, then write the module's documentation yourself.

Implemented for PostgreSQL, MariaDB and the ServiceNow Table API (Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.*); obtained via IDataSourceProviderResolver, never constructed directly outside DI registration.     QueryResult record 4 Generic, provider-agnostic row set returned by ExecuteAsync/ ExecuteNativeAsync. Every value is already stringified by the provider (e.g. a Postgres date/timestamp column is coerced to ISO-8601) so callers never need provider-specific type information; a null value means the source column was NULL. Each row's Values lines up index-for-index with Columns.

    SourceSchema record 4 The live (or demo-fallback) schema of the configured data source, as returned by ReadSchemaAsync/TestConnectionAsync.

    Components

    DataSourceCapabilities

    record · DataSourceCapabilities.cs

    What a provider can and can't do, stated explicitly — so callers and the shared provider contract tests branch on a named capability, never on provider.Type == …. Only differences that exist between the implemented providers are modeled; everything else in IDataSourceProvider (connection test, schema with relations, projection, filters, null checks, limit, joins, cancellation, sanitized errors) is required of every provider.

    Reached from: POST /api/export-definitions/{id:int}/preview, POST /api/export-definitions/{id:int}/run, POST /api/export-definitions/{id:int}/run-selected, POST /api/export-definitions/{id:int}/test, GET /api/pipeline/preview, POST /api/pipeline/run, POST /api/pipeline/run/{name}

    DataSourceConfig

    record · DataSourceConfig.cs

    Connection parameters for the configured ERP data source. Provider-agnostic by design: Type says which IDataSourceProvider (resolved via IDataSourceProviderResolver) interprets the rest of these fields — a relational source (PostgreSql/ MariaDb) uses Host/Port/Database, an HTTP API source (ServiceNowTableApi/ ServiceNowSqlApi) uses InstanceUrl instead. See knowledge/architecture/data-source-configuration.md for the full design and back-compat contract.

    Member Summary Derived from code Complexity
    ToString() Overridden so the compiler-generated, all-properties ToString() a bare record would otherwise get can never print Password in plaintext — e.g. into a log via / $"", or a debugger's default display. Redacts Password to a fixed marker and reports HasPassword instead, mirroring the API's own "hasPassword, never the value" contract. 1

    DataSourceQueryException

    class · DataSourceQueryException.cs

    Provider-agnostic wrapper for a query execution failure that a caller needs to inspect, not just log or surface verbatim — e.g. to recognize a specific SQL error without referencing Npgsql.PostgresException/ SqlState directly. ErrorCode is the provider's own error-code string verbatim (the Postgres SQLSTATE, for PostgreSqlDataSourceProvider) — opaque to callers unless they know the specific code they're looking for.

    Member Summary Derived from code Complexity
    ValidateConfig(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) Whether config has what this provider needs to connect (required fields, a valid TLS mode or instance URL): a user-facing message, or null when it's usable. Checked before any connection attempt; the only place per-source-type config rules live. 1
    TargetHost(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) The host a connection with the (validated) config reaches — what the SSRF check in POST /api/connection resolves. 1
    IsAlwaysEncrypted(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) True when config can only ever reach the source encrypted — never falling back to plaintext. 1
    TestConnectionAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Opens a connection against config and reads back its schema, without persisting anything. Never throws for a reachability/credential failure — that's reported via Success/Error instead, sanitized of any connection-string/credential detail. 1
    ReadSchemaAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Reads the live schema (tables/columns/PK/FK) of the data source described by config. Throws on failure — unlike TestConnectionAsync, this is called once a connection is already known-good and a failure here is a real, reportable error. 1
    ExecuteAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, Connector.Core.DataSources.SourceQuery, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Validates query against the data source's live schema (SourceQueryValidator), compiles it into the provider's own dialect with every filter value bound as a parameter, executes it, and returns its rows generically. Throws InvalidSourceQueryException — before touching any data — for an unknown table/column or a malformed query; an execution failure the caller needs to inspect surfaces as DataSourceQueryException. 1
    ExecuteNativeAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, Connector.Core.DataSources.NativeSqlQuery, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Executes caller-built, provider-native SQL as-is and returns its rows generically — the path DynamicExportService's JSON-tree builders still use for what SourceQuery cannot express yet (knowledge/architecture/source-query-model.md §5). Same error contract as ExecuteAsync, minus schema validation. 1

    SourceQuery

    record · SourceQuery.cs

    Database-neutral description of one read query: a root table, the columns to project, equi-joins to further tables, and AND-combined filter conditions. Carries no SQL at all — every table and column is a plain name that SourceQueryValidator checks against a known SourceSchema, and every filter value stays a value (never text spliced into a query), so a provider's compiler can always bind it as a parameter. Only providers know a dialect; the PostgreSQL one is Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.PostgreSql.PostgreSqlQueryCompiler. See knowledge/architecture/source-query-model.md.

    Linked tests: SourceQueryValidatorTests.Validate_ColumnOfTableThatIsNotJoined_Throws, SourceQueryValidatorTests.Validate_DuplicateOutputName_Throws, SourceQueryValidatorTests.Validate_JoinReferencingLaterJoin_Throws, SourceQueryValidatorTests.Validate_NegativeLimit_Throws, SourceQueryValidatorTests.Validate_TableJoinedTwice_Throws, SourceQueryValidatorTests.Validate_UnknownColumn_Throws, SourceQueryValidatorTests.Validate_UnknownJoinColumn_Throws, SourceQueryValidatorTests.Validate_UnknownRootTable_Throws, +41 more — test code that uses it, not coverage

    SourceQueryValidator

    class · SourceQueryValidator.cs

    Checks a SourceQuery against a known SourceSchema before any provider compiles it: every table and column must exist in the schema (matched exactly, case-sensitively), joins must build on the root table or an earlier join, every table appears at most once, output names are unique, and each condition's operand fits its operator. Dialect-free on purpose, so every provider's compiler shares it — a compiler may assume any query that passes is safe to turn into native syntax (every name it quotes is one the schema itself reported).

    Linked tests: SourceQueryValidatorTests.Validate (via SourceQueryValidator.Validate(SourceQuery, SourceSchema)) — test code that uses it, not coverage
